title: Unordered Map Contains C++20
description: Check if key exists in unordered_map (C++20)
explanation: contains() is the clearest way to check key existence in unordered_map.

title: Unordered Map Try Emplace C++17
description: Insert key-value pair only if key is absent (C++17)
explanation: try_emplace constructs the value in-place only if the key doesn't exist. Unlike emplace, it doesn't move from the key on failure.

title: Unordered Map Insert Or Assign
explanation: insert_or_assign either inserts a new element or assigns to an existing one.

title: Unordered Map Bucket Interface
explanation: The bucket interface allows inspection of the hash table internal structure.

title: Unordered Map Load Factor Control
description: Control hash table load factor for performance
explanation: Load factor = size/bucket_count. When exceeded, rehashing occurs. Lower load factor = faster lookups, more memory.

title: Unordered Map Custom Hash
description: Use a custom hash function with unordered_map
explanation: Custom hash functions enable using user-defined types as keys or optimizing hash distribution.

title: Unordered Map Reserving Space
explanation: Call reserve() when you know the number of elements ahead of time to avoid repeated rehashing.

title: Unordered Map Emplace
description: Construct key-value pair in-place in unordered_map
explanation: emplace constructs the pair in-place, potentially avoiding copies.

title: Unordered Map Extract C++17
description: Extract node from hash map without copying (C++17)
explanation: Extracts a node handle, allowing modification of the key and transfer between hash maps without copying.

title: Unordered Map Merge C++17
explanation: Transfers non-duplicate elements from one unordered_map to another without copying.

title: Unordered Map Float Key Warning
description: Warning about using floating-point types as keys
explanation: Using float/double as keys is problematic due to precision issues and NaN behavior.
